items.title: A second characterisation of injective modules through Baer's criterion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a characterisation of injectivity for modules over a ring in terms of ideals, and the proof is a 54-line argument that follows the classical route of Baer's criterion. It shows first that the extension property for all ideals implies the extension property for all inclusions by passing to a maximal counterexample and reducing to the case of a cyclic extension, and then verifies the criterion in the case that matters by an explicit construction with the annihilator of an element. The reduction to the maximal counterexample and the explicit extension are both written out.
